gen-righteous-noto-serif: Righteous bends every letter like thin rod, bowls filling the line. Noto Serif moves at a gentler reading pace, its mild thick-thin rhythm and prominent x-height making paragraphs easy to settle into, where the heading just shouts in smooth outline.
gen-shadows-into-light-bitter: Bitter reads dependable and grounded, with a very large lowercase eye and a visible gap in each s. And the handwritten Shadows Into Light adds the friendly, chalk-crowded charm, which is exactly what that slab-serif lacks.
gen-shadows-into-light-inter: Loose, chalky and casual. Inter follows in a plain sans with breathing counters and a smooth tube-like line, though a heading made small would lose Shadows Into Light's wide-mouthed rounds.
gen-shadows-into-light-poppins: Friendly handwriting leads, with wide-mouthed rounds in the lowercase, while Poppins keeps its curves round and its lowercase tall and sturdy. Paragraphs run smooth, without any thick-thin flicker.
gen-silkscreen-gf-cascadia-code: Silkscreen leaves space around every letter, a lo-fi line you can almost feel. Cascadia Code answers with a wire-like monoline skeleton and a taller lowercase, so the retro pixel heading sits above a smoother, more modern text.
gen-silkscreen-gf-cascadia-mono: Pixel-retro up top, tidy below. Cascadia Mono stands its letters like pins with curves as thick as its stems, and that compact skyline is the strongest thing it brings next to Silkscreen.
gen-silkscreen-gf-julius-sans-one: Julius Sans One reads light and open, with capitals and lowercase nearly level. Its big stretches of blank space between letters echo the spacing of Silkscreen, and that shared looseness is the strongest thing tying them.
gen-silkscreen-gf-lexend-exa: Silkscreen spaces out every letter in a lo-fi, retro line like spaghetti. But Lexend Exa has a thickness that never shifts with direction and a big x-height, so the heading looks quirky and the text steady.
gen-silkscreen-gf-lexend-giga: Retro pixels meet flat, single-weight lines. Lexend Giga opens each word with generous tracking and keeps its ascenders close to the x-height, so a long page would move along smoothly, one even step after another.
gen-silkscreen-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega reads approachable, drawn with one nib and nearly capital-tall lowercase. Silkscreen sets the lo-fi tone above it, and the moderate-to-high height jump gives the two a clear step between them.
